problem: Let $f$ be a function such that ${f}^{′}(x)=12{x}^{2}-6$ and $f(1)=-2.$ Use the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=1$ to estimate the value of $f(2).$
worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(1)=-2,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=12{x}^{2}-6,$ then ${f}^{′}(1)=12(1)^{2}-6=6.$ So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=-2+6(x-1).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(2)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & ≈L(2) \\  & =-2+6(2-1) \\  & =-2+6(1) \\  & =-2+6 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
